key_insight: The paper proposes that coherent ferromagnetic magnons could bypass mass dilution and nuclear spin cancellation that constrain phonon-mediated nuclear resonance energy transfer in metal deuterides.
engineering_relevance: If validated, this mechanism could guide magnetic excitation strategies that avoid the lattice-fracture constraints of phonon-driven energy transfer.
method: Extend a generalized nuclear Dicke model to ferromagnetic-resonance magnons.
Combine hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling with Overhauser-polarized Dirac M2 coupling.
Derive a Suhl-clamped ferromagnetic-resonance scaling law.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical predictions of 14.2 MeV neutrons for Pd-106, 11.4 MeV neutrons for Ni-58, and 19.9 MeV alpha particles, but describes no experimental validation.
watch_item: The predicted nuclear energy transfer requires experimental verification under achievable magnon coherence and nuclear spin polarization.
paper_title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
